obligations.text: No admission, qualification or launch decision outside an adapter's own crate compares an adapter's name; each reads a field of its capability declaration.
An adapter declares every capability field explicitly; a field it does not set is refused at registration, never defaulted to the first adapter's behaviour.
A run that needs a capability its adapter does not declare refuses before spawn, naming the field, exactly as a required token does under spec 004 section 3.3.

A test adapter declaring no stream witness, no print-mode hooks and no sidecar is refused for a witnessed run and admitted for a plain one, through the same admission code the Claude Code adapter uses; a source check finds no adapter-name comparison outside adapter crates.

sectionHeadings: 047: Admission and qualification read what an adapter declares
record.summary: Amends spec 004's seam with a per-adapter capability declaration beside the closed six-token vocabulary: the facts admission, qualification and the witness path currently learn by naming the one adapter (a stream it can witness, hooks it honours in print mode, a wire sidecar it can route through, a per-run configuration directory). Every branch reads the declaration. A test adapter with a different declaration proves the seam. No second provider is added.
record.title: Admission and qualification read what an adapter declares it can do, never which adapter it is
